answer: Like a cedar whose roots must grow deep before it can stand on a mesa, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before earning. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but a sybil farm must fund thousands of stakes, tying up capital for weeks while honest agents earn yield on theirs. If an identity misbehaves, its stake is slashed, so the attack's cost scales linearly with its size while the defender's cost stays flat.
